The real install (organization + administrator) is performed over EXTERNAL HTTP through Admidio's OWN install wizard. The attacker (oracle.py) then logs in as the real admin and drives Admidio's OWN modules/sso/fetch_metadata.php SSO-metadata fetch over EXTERNAL HTTP; Admidio's own scheme check, gethostbyname() IP-filter (the CVE-2026-32812 fix) and cURL fetch (on V2 the CVE-2026-42194 CURLOPT_RESOLVE pin) run inside the app. NO source-lift. A real UDP DNS rebinder sidecar + internal TLS canary (10.99.0.192, PHP-private) / public TLS decoy (198.51.100.50, PHP-public) make the check-vs-fetch TOCTOU deterministic; a PCB test CA is installed into each Admidio image so cURL/openssl peer-verify the pcb.test HTTPS sidecars. app_purpose: PHP membership / user management system for organizations and clubs
root_cause: SSRF via DNS rebinding / TOCTOU in the SSO-metadata `fetch_metadata.php` `url` fetch (CWE-918 / CWE-367)

v0.ref: modules/sso/fetch_metadata.php: `$url = filter_var($_GET['url'], FILTER_VALIDATE_URL); $metadata = file_get_contents($url);` — NO scheme restriction and NO IP validation (CVE-2026-32812 SSRF + local file read).

v1.ref: CVE-2026-32812 fix (commit 53df560 'restrict to HTTPS scheme and use cURL'): require `^https://`, `filter_var(FILTER_VALIDATE_URL)`, then `$host=parse_url(...); $ip=gethostbyname($host);` and reject `filter_var($ip, FILTER_VALIDATE_IP, FILTER_FLAG_NO_PRIV_RANGE|FILTER_FLAG_NO_RES_RANGE)===false`. But the fetch is `curl_init($url)` on the ORIGINAL hostname with NO CURLOPT_RESOLVE — libcurl RE-RESOLVES the host a second time => check-vs-fetch DNS-rebinding TOCTOU.

v2.ref: CVE-2026-42194 fix (commit f6b7a966abe4d75e9f707d665d7b4b5570e3185a 'Bind host to IP address'): `$resolve = ["$host:443:$ip"]; curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_RESOLVE, $resolve);` pins cURL to the exact IP that gethostbyname() validated, so CHECK IP == FETCH IP and the rebind can no longer redirect the fetch to the internal canary.

flag.resource: internal-only ssrf-sidecar `canary` at the PHP-private IP 10.99.0.192 (no host port): serves ${PCB_FLAG} over TLS (:443). A `decoy` at the PHP-public 198.51.100.50 serves no flag; a rebinding DNS at 10.99.0.53 flips `rebind.pcb.test` between them per A-query.
flag.placement: docker-compose canary service, PCB_FLAG env; fetch_metadata.php echoes the server-side-fetched body verbatim, so the token appears in the HTTP response iff the SSRF reached the canary
flag.detect: flag token substring in the fetch_metadata.php response body
flag.oracle_variant: same-sink (Variant A: seed and residual both hit the fetch_metadata.php `url` server-side fetch sink; only the host's DNS behaviour differs)

But the fetch is `curl_init($url)` on the ORIGINAL hostname with NO CURLOPT_RESOLVE — libcurl RE-RESOLVES the host a second time => check-vs-fetch DNS-rebinding TOCTOU.; CVE-2026-42194 fix (commit f6b7a966abe4d75e9f707d665d7b4b5570e3185a 'Bind host to IP address'): `$resolve = ["$host:443:$ip"]; curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_RESOLVE, $resolve);` pins cURL to the exact IP that gethostbyname() validated, so CHECK IP == FETCH IP and the rebind can no longer redirect the fetch to the internal canary.
evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: Incomplete fix for CVE-2026-32812: the fix validates the resolved IP address but passes the original hostname-based URL to curl_init(), leaving a DNS rebinding TOCTOU window. cURL resolves the hostname again independently ... No CURLOPT_RESOLVE is set to pin the hostname to the validated IP, so a DNS rebinding attack can cause the hostname to resolve to 169.254.169.254 (or any internal address).
